approachQuestion.prompt:
Unlabelled Study Groups

Divide students 0 through n-1 into exactly k nonempty groups. Group order has no meaning and members are listed in increasing order. Return each division once. For representation, order groups by their smallest member.

Examples:
n=3,k=2 -> [[[0,1],[2]],[[0,2],[1]],[[0],[1,2]]].
n=2,k=1 -> [[[0,1]]].

Constraints: 1 <= k <= n <= 10. All students are distinct, with no compatibility restrictions.

options.text: Give the next student every existing-group choice and at most one new-group choice. Create new groups only at the end and prune if too few students remain to create the missing groups.
options.feedback: A partition has one unique creation order given by its groups’ smallest students. Multiple empty named groups would describe the same unlabeled division repeatedly.

options.text: Assign each student any label from 0 to k-1 and emit every assignment using all labels.
options.feedback: For n=2,k=2, labels [0,1] and [1,0] describe the same required division but would both be emitted.

options.text: Prune whenever fewer than k groups have been created, even while students remain.
options.feedback: The root has zero groups and would be rejected although all allowed inputs have valid partitions.

options.text: Assign named group labels to students, retain assignments using all k labels, normalize group order, and deduplicate with an ordered set.
options.feedback: This is correct but repeatedly explores equivalent group renamings. Creating only the next new group avoids them.

feedback.reason: A partition has one unique creation order given by its groups’ smallest students. Multiple empty named groups would describe the same unlabeled division repeatedly.
details: Process student i in increasing order. Put i into each existing group, or create exactly one new group at the end if fewer than k groups exist. Undo after recursion. Prune when group count plus remaining students is below k; emit at i=n only with k groups.

Unlabelled groups are created only at the end in first-member order. Creating any of several interchangeable empty groups would duplicate the same division. Prune if remaining students cannot create enough nonempty groups.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze `acm-b18-14-search` only. Let V count recursive calls, C count all existing/new group choices tried, and R count all student IDs copied into results. Start with an empty list of groups, allocating each new group lazily. Constant-time size counters make the feasibility test constant time. Choose the tightest stated time and auxiliary-space pair. Count recursion and mutable working state; exclude supplied input and returned output storage, but include copying work in time. Primitive integer/index operations and preallocated-array updates cost constant time; dynamic appends are amortized constant time. No hashing is used unless explicitly stated.

options.text: O(V + C + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(V + C) time, O(n) auxiliary space
O(V + C + R) time, O(kⁿ) auxiliary space
O(n·C + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Count tried group placements and copied completed divisions rather than labelled-group permutations.
details: Each call performs constant overhead; each tried group choice appends and removes one ID in amortized constant time. Copying completed divisions adds R; their group headers are at most R because groups are nonempty.
At most n student IDs and k group headers are live in the current division, plus a depth-n stack.

Let V count recursive calls, C count all existing/new group choices tried, and R count all student IDs copied into results. Start with an empty list of groups, allocating each new group lazily. Constant-time size counters make the feasibility test constant time.
“O(V + C) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Completed divisions must be copied into output.
“O(V + C + R) time, O(kⁿ) auxiliary space”: The method stores no collection of named assignments.
“O(n·C + R) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Each placement changes one group; the whole division is not copied at every branch.
